doc.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995

title: Lurlean with Johnny Long, Les Hite and a Lake Vaughan job
summary: Williams sang with Lurlean in Johnny Long's band and worked near Les Hite at a summer resort in 1940; Terry adds Ellington's ideal singer.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: You know it took me a long time to figure out who ... she sounded like an extension of Ivie Anderson, you know, really, a real extension, because she was smooth. We sang with Johnny Long’s band together you know.
Yeah. We did the dancing, we’d dance in between numbers when we weren’t singing, we’d dance together.
I thought you were going to say Les Hite. She used to sing.

No. I worked with Les, but she wasn’t with him. He had let’s see what is it, Bobbie somebody was playing piano with him, a girl, a black girl named Bobbie something. And I’ve forgotten the girl singer he had, but when he came to Chicago, he had T-Bone Walker with him at the Regal Theater I remember, but I worked with him up in a place in Delavan, Wisconsin called Lake Vaughan during the summer one summer he was up there. I was the head waiter, I was a waiter up there at night, and in the daytime I was the porter, and I was cleaning up. I was going through a bad time with a love affair.

No, no. This was my first lady, my first love man. She was putting me through it and I was going for it. So I was working two jobs, saving money. I learned a lot, oooh, the lessons I learned from that, man. You know like my parents, they laid it on me during that period because I had two or three hundred dollars, this was 1940. And I had two or three hundred dollars of my own, so I gave the money to them, “here, hold this money for me.” And they told me, keep my own money.

When you mentioned that Lurlean sounded a little bit like Ivie Anderson, it made me think Duke Ellington always said that his idea of the perfect singer was one who sounded like Ivie Anderson and looked like Lena Horne.
